text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are suffering from severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and dysuria. To help me narrow down the cause, have you noticed any fever or chills accompanying these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID).

Based on your history of dysuria, severe abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and the burning pain during intercourse, you have symptoms highly suggestive of an infection spreading from your lower urinary tract or reproductive organs. Given your age, sexual activity, and inconsistent condom use, this is likely due to sexually transmitted bacteria like Chlamydia or Gonorrhea. We will need to confirm this with specific tests to determine the exact cause and prescribe the correct antibiotics.
